root_cause.text: Use of 32-bit `unsigned int` variables (`block_offset` and `delta`) in `__rdma_block_iter_next()` causes integer overflow when reassembling large DMA blocks (>=4GB) from split SG entries, leading to incorrect DMA address computation.
root_cause.evidence: The patch changes these variables to `dma_addr_t` to fix the truncation; the commit message explicitly states "overflowing the 32 bit stack values and computed the wrong DMA addresses".

candidates.rationale: Function entry point for the vulnerable iteration logic; the overflow occurs inside this function due to the use of 32-bit unsigned integers.
32-bit unsigned int declaration that can overflow when computing addresses for blocks >=4GB, leading to incorrect DMA address calculation.

Early exit when no SG entries; if entries exist, the overflow-prone calculations proceed, making this line a branching point that leads to vulnerable execution.

vuln_statements.explanation: 32-bit unsigned integer declaration that overflows when computing addresses for blocks >=4GB, leading to incorrect DMA address calculation in the block iteration loop.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
RDMA: Move DMA block iterator logic into dedicated files

The DMA iterator logic was mixed into verbs and umem-specific
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 6094ea64c69520ed1e770e7c79c43412de202bfa
Author: Leon Romanovsky <leon@kernel.org>
Date:   Fri Feb 13 12:57:37 2026 +0200

    RDMA: Move DMA block iterator logic into dedicated files
    
    The DMA iterator logic was mixed into verbs and umem-specific code,
    forcing all users to include rdma/ib_umem.h. Move the block iterator
    logic into iter.c and rdma/iter.h so that rdma/ib_umem.h and
    rdma/ib_verbs.h can be separated in a follow-up patch.
    
    Link: https://patch.msgid.
bic_trace_step.reason: The function uses 'unsigned int' for 'block_offset' and 'delta'. When page size is >=4GB, BIT_ULL(biter->__pg_bit) can exceed 32-bit range; subtracting block_offset and assigning to unsigned int delta truncates the value, causing integer overflow (e.g., delta becomes 0 for 4GB pages). This leads to incorrect while-loop condition and DMA address computation, matching the vulnerability root cause.
